details:
Project Details: SPHEREx Explorer

SPHEREx Explorer is a free, bilingual web application designed to make NASA's SPHEREx infrared sky survey interactive, accessible, and understandable to everyone. It allows users to search for any celestial object or sky coordinate and retrieve its available SPHEREx observations, arranged chronologically and by wavelength.

How It Works

The application connects directly to NASA/IPAC's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) through its SIA2 image search, cutout service, and AWS S3 cloud mirror. Users can explore observations through an interactive timeline and blink consecutive images to identify changes in the sky, following the same visual technique historically used by astronomers such as Clyde Tombaugh.

Beyond visualization, SPHEREx Explorer implements an automated moving-object detection pipeline. It identifies potential moving points across image sequences and cross-matches them with NASA JPL's Small-Body Identification API (SBIdent) and Horizons ephemeris predictions to identify known asteroids and comets. For example, our system identified asteroid (7) Iris passing near 36 Sextantis in December 2025, with its observed position matching JPL's prediction within 0.8 arcseconds.

A key scientific consideration is that SPHEREx observes the sky across different infrared wavelengths. Therefore, the application compares brightness measurements only between observations at matching wavelengths, preventing spectral differences from being misinterpreted as changes in brightness. It also provides historical comparisons using AllWISE, 2MASS, and Digitized Sky Survey imagery spanning approximately 75 years.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project lowers the technical barrier to astronomical exploration by bringing complex scientific archives into an accessible interface. Students, educators, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts can investigate celestial objects, compare historical observations, identify known moving objects, and understand how the infrared sky changes over time. The bilingual English-Bangla interface further expands accessibility, particularly for Bangla-speaking communities.

Our intended impact is to encourage public participation in astronomy, strengthen scientific literacy, and demonstrate how publicly available NASA data can be transformed into meaningful, interactive scientific experiences.

Technologies and Data Sources

The project integrates:

  • NASA SPHEREx: Quick Release 2 and 3 spectral images from Wide and Deep surveys.
  • NASA/IPAC IRSA: SIA2 image search, cutout service, and AWS S3 cloud mirror.
  • NASA JPL Solar System Dynamics: SBIdent API and Horizons for asteroid and comet identification and orbital predictions.
  • CDS HiPS2FITS: SPHEREx all-sky maps and historical AllWISE and 2MASS imagery.
  • CDS SIMBAD and Sesame: Astronomical object identification and contextual information.
  • Digitized Sky Survey (STScI): Historical Palomar photographic plates.
  • Web technologies: Interactive frontend, astronomical image processing, API integration, and AI-assisted question answering.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of SPHEREx Explorer lies in combining multiple astronomical capabilities into one unified exploration experience. Rather than simply displaying static astronomical images, it turns the sky into a time-based, multi-wavelength investigation environment.

We incorporated the historical blink-comparison technique, automated moving-object detection, scientific cross-validation, a gamified "Spot the Mover" experience, and a bilingual AI assistant that cites its sources.

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy, wavelength consistency, data provenance, accessibility, and transparency. We also considered the limitations of astronomical image comparisons, the reliability of moving-object identification, and the importance of distinguishing confirmed observations from potential discoveries.

Most importantly, SPHEREx Explorer never claims an independent astronomical discovery. It presents real observational data, provides verifiable scientific references, and helps users investigate the universe without overstating what the data demonstrates.
